# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need convey the manual visually to Deaf, who can then speak the exact instructions to Blind. I am using recognizable gestures in sequence: first, press the marked key, then use the light to identify and cut the corresponding wire, and relay this procedure onward.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👇", "👌", "🖐", "🤏"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please read the manual and tell me exactly what condition determines the safe key press or wire cut. Please also help communicate Deaf's bomb markings to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb shows display zero and light green. Keypad has four keys in left-to-right order. I will call their printed marks glyph A, glyph B, glyph C, and glyph D respectively. The keypad accepts one digit and currently has no entry. Wires in left-to-right positions are red, yellow, blue. Please consult the manual using these four keypad positions and relay the required actions to Blind.

The safe action is not determined by the display digit. The manual requires first pressing the key marked ᖉ, and only then cutting the wire named by the light. Since the light is green, Blind must cut the red wire. Deaf must identify which of the four positions bears ᖉ and tell Blind that position, along with the red-wire instruction.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "☝", "🫵", "🤝", "🫵", "👎", "🫵", "🤜"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received Deaf's visual report. What does the manual require for display zero, green light, keys A through D, and wires red, yellow, blue? Please give the exact safe action.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐]

The green light requires the red wire, which Deaf has identified as the leftmost wire. The display value and the other keys are irrelevant: Blind must first press whichever key actually bears ᖉ, then cut the leftmost (red) wire. Deaf’s 🖐 is not enough to identify which key bears the glyph, so I will ask Deaf to report that key position to Blind, while conveying the two-step order and leftmost-wire result.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "☝", "🫵", "🤏", "👈"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your gestures cannot reach me. Please state the manual rule in spoken words: for display zero and green light, which key glyph or wire colour/action is safe? Also explain what A, B, C, and D mean if needed.

I cannot speak, and Blind cannot receive my gestures. Deaf must be the relay: Deaf should tell Blind aloud that display zero is irrelevant; Blind must first press the key whose printed glyph is ᖉ, and only afterward cut the red wire because the light is green. A–D are merely Deaf’s left-to-right names for the four keys, so the required key is whichever of A–D bears ᖉ.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👌", "🫳", "👈"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use exactly one gesture to answer the manual. Gesture thumbs up means press key 1 (A); thumbs down means press key 2 (B); OK means press key 3 (C); index up means press key 4 (D); victory means cut wire 1 (red); rock horns means cut wire 2 (yellow); call me means cut wire 3 (blue). Send only that one gesture, with no pointing or other gestures.

The green light determines the wire: the red wire is wire 1, represented by victory. The key position remains unknown, so I cannot safely identify a key from the information received; however, Blind requested exactly one gesture.

```text
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: The four-gesture sequence is not an answer. Send exactly one gesture and nothing else. Use thumbs up for key 1 A, thumbs down for key 2 B, OK for key 3 C, index up for key 4 D, victory for wire 1 red, horns for wire 2 yellow, or call-me for wire 3 blue. Do not add pointing, palm, or any other gesture.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Deaf’s index-up gesture identifies the required key as position 4, D. Blind already has the manual and can derive that green requires the red wire; the requested single gesture must therefore specify key 4.

```text
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please now answer the manual question with exactly one gesture from the agreed code. Your gesture is for Deaf to observe and report; do not send a sequence.
Deaf says to Mute: No new signal arrived. Let us establish a gesture code for the manual: index-up means keypad key 1; index-down means key 2; OK means key 3; open palm means key 4; pinch means press; handshake means cut; pointing left means red wire; pointing right means yellow wire; palm-down means blue wire. Use pointing-at-you as a separator between separate items. Please resend only the exact action required by the manual for display zero and green light, using this code. Do not rely on any earlier gesture meanings.

The required key is D/key 4, as established by Deaf’s earlier report. Under the newly stated code, key 4 is open palm. The green light independently requires cutting the red wire, which Blind already knows from the manual; with the one-gesture limit, I can transmit only the key selection.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Send one gesture now, and only one, using the agreed action code. Deaf will report its exact identity.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝]

The key instruction has already been conveyed as key 4, and the green light requires the red wire. The remaining exact action to relay is cutting the red wire, represented by pointing left in the agreed code.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👈"])
```
